quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you may pass.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral as you drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your headlights to high beam.
Turn your headlights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: You should allow extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
A small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers may not see you behind them. Increase your distance to see around these vehicles and ahead on the road.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors and blind spots for vehicles. Always signal before changing lanes to give others time to react.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: A yellow light warns that red is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the road center mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots. Do not drive beside them for long stretches.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: To let other drivers merge onto the freeway.
To give the truck driver enough room to stop.
To help other drivers when they slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give the truck driver enough room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Never pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of colors on a traffic light?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights have red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom. Red means stop, yellow means caution, and green means go.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road. An oncoming vehicle is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to tell the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one road hazard at a time. When you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams will bounce back at you and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back and create glare that makes it hard to see ahead.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for hazards. Staring only at the road right in front of you is dangerous. Scan ahead and watch the vehicles around you.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may happen?

options.text: The truck may complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
The truck may have to swing wide to complete the turn.
The truck must stay in the right lane at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may have to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the back wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need to swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: When you see this road sign, what should you do?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: To pass safely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. Always check that you have enough space to change lanes safely before passing. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes and you have a clear view of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder. This ensures no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no other drivers are moving into the same spot.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: In order to see potential hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In order to see potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic conditions. Look for signals from other drivers. Watch for vehicles entering at on-ramps and be ready for changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks if you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: A pentagon-shaped sign is a:

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about a school zone. These signs alert you that children or pedestrians may be crossing nearby.

questions.question: A curb painted red means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.
